entry.dc:title: Main Lines of Intensification of the Making of Large Open Pit Mining Machines.
entry.dc:creator: Daskovskii V.
entry.dc:description: At present, the Soviet stock of open-pit mining machinery includes rotary bucket excavators with the capacity of 5000 m**3/h and with the mass of 4850 t; walking dredgers with 100 m long jibs and with 25 m**3 buckets, with the mass of 2200 t; mechanical spades with 65 m long jibs and 35 m**3 bucket, with the mass of 2700 t; open jet excavators with 12. 5 m**3 buckets. It takes from 50 to 65 months to design and make a 2000-3000 t machine. The article considers the problem of how to speed up the designing and making of large machinery for open-pit prices in order to save costs. Examples from the assembly site at the Nikopol manganese ore mining basin are given to illustrate the problems involved.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPING AND OPERATING A MAMMOTH QUARRY.
entry.dc:creator: Yeoman J.
entry.dc:description: The Foster Yeoman company started quarrying in Somerset back in 1922, the quarry occupying a central position in the 30-mile length of the Mendip Hills. The whole range of Mendip is from Weston-super-Mare to Frome, all Carboniferous limestone with markets then and now away to the south and south-east. The article considers the application of the concepts of open pit mining to the quarrying industry.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT MINING AND THE DREDGE.
entry.dc:creator: Turner T.

entry.dc:title: DIGGING DEEP FOR COPPER.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Rio Tinto's Edward Hunt is convinced that most future mineral discoveries will be deeper than those found in the past. When open pit mining ceases in about 17 years from now, the plan is to go underground with a production rate of 50 000 t a day. Nothing like this has been attempted before in South Africa. The proposed method will be a form of sub-level open stoping with delayed pillar recovery, giving a high overall extraction. At the projected mining grade and recovery, 50 000 t a day would yield about 90 000 t of copper a year which is comparable with present production. The article is an interview.

entry.dc:title: AIR BLAST AND GROUND VIBRATION IN OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Andrews A.B.
entry.dc:description: Using the basic timing guidelines for blast design given, results of this experimental work using sequential initiation to provide timing flexibility showed the following: The peak particle velocity and frequency of ground motion were unaffected by changes in timing over the range investigated. Blasts of short duration produced ground motion of shorter duration and less energy. The shorter duration of the motion reduces public annoyance. The smaller amount of seismic energy was accompanied by an increase in burden displacement. Air blast was associated with the transmission of a portion of the stress wave into the air upon reflection at the free face from the firing of the first row of holes. The absence of air blast from subsequent rows was noted. Superposition of air blast pulses can be minimized by controlling the rate of blast progression along the free face. The simultaneous firing of opening holes is to be avoided if air blast is a problem.

entry.dc:title: Basic Concepts of Automated Open Pit Mining System Projects.
entry.dc:creator: Kusnezow K.
entry.dc:description: A man-machine system aimed at higher technology and effectiveness is offered. Better projecting and calculating procedures are suggested to cut costs. Diagrams show improved methods.

entry.dc:title: Open Pit Method of Mining Ferruginous Quartizites in the Krivoi Rog Basin.
entry.dc:creator: Statkevich A.A.
entry.dc:description: Between 1955 and 1968 five ore-dressing combines have been built in the Krivoi Rog basin. They treat ferruginous quartzites mined from 9 large open pit mines whose projected depth reaches 300-500 m and annual capacity from 5 to 36 million t of crude ore. The annual capacity of the combines is: 135 Mt of crude ore and 60 Mt of concentrate with the iron content of 64-65%. The article gives a brief description of all the combines of the open pit mining methods, transportation, waste disposal and recultivation of the stripped soil. Plans to deepen open pit mines to 450, 500 and even 800 m are outlined. A project of construction of a super-ore-dressing combine with the capacity of 150-180 Mt of crude ore per annum with an open pit mine 900-1000 m deep is mentioned.

entry.dc:title: USE OF BELT CONVEYORS IN OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: St. John C.
entry.dc:description: The use of belt conveyors in one of the largest stripping operations in the history of mining, at Twin Buttes near Tucson, Arizona, is described. The present alluvium handling system consists of two 60-in. belt conveyors, 2,400 and 3,000 ft. long each, designed to handle 8,000 tph. The conveyors will be extended and a new one added in 1975. This new belt is to be both shiftable and extendable. Designed with modular construction in mind, it will be extended 20 times in increments of 256 ft each and will be moved 25 times in its 10-year life span. A new 11,500 ft conveying system planned for the mine is described. There are also a few miles of conveyors handling crushed ore bearing rock.

entry.dc:title: OPTIMIZING OPEN PIT MINING WITH COMPUTER SIMULATION.
entry.dc:creator: Butler J.
entry.dc:description: The Wabco simulation program is described which provides an approach to solve open pit mining production and planning problems by using the computer to simulate the thousands of events that take place simultaneously in the pit. Program inputs and outputs, such as those concerning information about shovels, trucks, dumps and crushers, haul profile, etc. and program mechanics are explained. Several examples of application are given.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: A survey is given of the developments in the field of open pit mining in 1974. The use of computers in the area of mine planning, new drilling hardware, blasting products, large-capacity tracks for haulage, tractor shovels, mining shovels and draglines is reviewed. some new projects are discussed briefly.

entry.dc:title: PLAN GEOMETRY AND OTHER FACTORS RELATING TO NATURAL ROCK SLOPE STABILITY APPLIED TO DESIGN OF DE BEERS MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Piteau D.F.
entry.dc:description: As part of a major study relating to the stability of rock slopes of De Beers Mine, a detailed investigation was made of the natural slopes of De Beers Mine and four other mines in Kimberley. Attempt was made to determine the controlling factors which either lead to or detract from the stability of the slopes, the main objective being to assess whether the natural breakback of the slopes would jeopardize the main railway line located in close proximity to the pit. Current theories of slope stability all deal with a slope as a two-dimensional problem, i. e. a slice of unit length of an infinitely long slope is considered for a condition of plane strain. In this the tacit assumption is made that the plan radii of the crest and toe of the slope are infinite. This is not the condition encountered in practice, particularly in open pit mining where these radii of curvature have important effects on the safe slope angles. To determine these and other effects a study was made of the slope breakback and other related factors in the four big holes of the diamond mines in the Kinberley area. Other forms of analyses of the basic radius of curvature and breakback data are conducted. It is shown that the major dimensions of the pipes are also important factors for the stability of these slopes. Based on simple experiments the mechanics of failure are determined and also factors such as comparison of effects of plan radius of curvature on the upper and lower parts of the slopes and possible effects of regional stress are assessed.

entry.dc:title: ROCK MECHANICS IN OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Brawner C.O.
entry.dc:description: The majority of information contained in past International Rock Mechanics Conferences has dealt with rock mechanics as applied in the field of civil engineering. In reality, more than 80 percent of all rock excavated throughout the world is associated with mining projects. During the past decade the mining industry has recognized the economic and safety implications of the application of rock mechanics to mining. As a result, numerous advances have been developed and implemented in data collection, property determination, theoretical analysis and field instrumentation. This supplementary report outlines briefly the general approach now being taken to assess the stability of rock slopes on mining projects. The most important factors which influence stability are the presence, orientation and shear strength of structural geologic discontinuities, groundwater pressures and influence of seismic acceleration forces due to frequent blasting. To illustrate the importance of typical variables, five case examples are described. They include two coal mines, one uranium mine, one copper mine and one asbestos mine. On the latter project a slide involving 35,000,000 tons was stabilized.

entry.dc:title: SCALE DEPOSITS UPSET BALL MILL WATER SERVICE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Heavy scale deposits within control valves at one of the world's largest open pit mining operations increased maintenance, and affected mill production until operations staff found an economical valve solution. The scaling on the discharge end of the ball mills caused critical production interruptions within three months of the mine's opening.

entry.dc:title: Experts' Evaluation of the Development of the Techniques and Technology of Iron Ore Open Pit Mining in the USSR by the Year 2000.
entry.dc:creator: Shtukaturov K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The role of experts' evaluation in compiling long-term forecasts is pointed out, the principles of composition of the questionnaries are formulated, and the mathematical tools for the treatment of answers are presented. Results of an opinion poll carried out in 1971-72 among open-pit mining and mining engineering specialists about the development of the techniques and technology of open pit iron ore mines in the USSR by the year 2000 are discussed.

entry.dc:title: From the Experience of Operation of the Sokolovsko-Sarbayskiy Ore-Dressing Combine.
entry.dc:creator: Pap
entry.dc:description: A series of 18 articles published on the occasion of the 20th anniversary of the iron-ore dressing combine describes the achievements of the combine over the two decades, the growth of output, open pit mining works, the technical progress, the mining and ore separating machinery, mechanization of auxiliary works, automation and centralized traffic control, ore separation, economics and organization of production, and introduction of automatic control systems. The output of the combine is 28 million t of crude ore per annum and the output of marketable ore is 15 million t, i. e. over 7% of its total output in the USSR. The ore is mined by open pit methods from the depth of between 35 and 120 m. The total ore resources are estimated at 2 billion t. The newly built mining city of Rudnyy has 100,000 inhabitants.

entry.dc:title: Future of Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Mel'nikov N.V.
entry.dc:description: Future developments in ore mining methods in the USSR are considered and various predictions are made. Increases in the share of open pit mining, and in the capacities of coal mines to 1. 5-2. 0 million t, and of iron ore mines to 8-10 million t and more, are envisaged. Increase of the depth of underground iron ore mines to 1500 m and of open pit mines to 500-600 m, and problems of ventilation, safety, transportation are outlined. Mining technology and mining machinery, application of geotechnological methods, offshore mining, waste disposal, recultivation of soils, etc. are considered and technological forecasts are made.

entry.dc:title: LU-CJA-TO COAL MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Lezon M.
entry.dc:description: With an annual output estimated at some 400 million mtons, the Chinese People's Republic is the world's third largest producer of coal after the U. S. S. R. and the U. S. A. The country's reserves are believed to total well over 1 multiplied by 10**1**2 mtons and the country is more reliant on coal as its major fuel source than perhaps any other. Most of the known deposits are comparatively close to surface, and both underground and open pit mining methods are used, but on balance, the mines tend to be smaller and less technologically advanced than their Western counterparts. In many of the underground properties there is little mechanization, but some of the larger underground units are hydraulic method, both in actual mining by water jet and in underground transportation of coal.

entry.dc:title: HAMERSLEY IRON.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Hamersly is currently Australia's largest iron ore producer with operations at Mt. Tom Price and Paraburdoo in the Pilbara area of Western Australia. Within 10 years from the initial discovery of the deposit, the company's iron ore output capacity had reached 22. 5 million ton/year and with the opening of the new Paraburdoo deposit, capacity is scheduled for 40 million ton/year by end-1974. A monographic description discusses: the geology of the deposit; open pit mining operations; haulage; comminution at Mt. Tom Price and Paraburdoo; pelletizing; transportation of ore by a 244 m long railway to Port Dampier; port facilities and further expansion program.

entry.dc:title: Some Experience of the Operation of the Kachkanarskiy Ore-Dressing Combine.
entry.dc:creator: Rev
entry.dc:description: Under the above general title, a series of 13 articles by many authors present a review of various aspects of the operation of the Kachkanarskiy ore-mining and ore-dressing combine in the Middle Urals, which was put into operation in 1964. Design capacity of the combine was 33 million t of raw ore, 5. 8 million t of the concentrate, 2. 7 million t of agglomerate, 2. 8 million t of pellets, and it was achieved approximately in 1973. A second combine for 45 million t of raw ore is planned, and the existing combine is to be expanded to handle 40 million t of raw ore. The raw material base of the combine, the development of open pit mining, explosion work, equipment of the combine, maintenance of diesel-electric locomotives, power supply, control and automation of technological processes, improvement of separation technology, production of the agglomerate and pellets, scientific organization of labor, chemical analysis of ores, etc, are dealt with in different articles.

entry.dc:title: Materials Handling at the Leipzig Spring Fair 1973.
entry.dc:creator: Engels H.
entry.dc:description: Review and description of some of the recent eshibited machinery in the field of materials handling. Considered are: equipment for open pit mining, container reloading equipment, and cranes.

entry.dc:title: COMPUTER SIMULATION OF TRACTOR-SCRAPER OPERATIONS IN WASTE STRIPPING.
entry.dc:creator: Thieme M.
entry.dc:description: A simulation model developed to analyze scraper-pusher utilization in open pit mining systems is described. The mining simulator discussed was developed as a tool to aid management in evaluating alternative open pit haulage schemes and to reduce the risk involved in the selection of equipment.

entry.dc:title: PHOSPHATE IN THE KOLA PENINSULA, USSR.
entry.dc:creator: Woodrooffe H.
entry.dc:description: Physical conditions of underground and open pit mining and flotation concentration from large reserves on Russia's Kola Peninsula north of the Arctic Circle are described. Current production capacity and future expansion figures are given.

entry.dc:title: Automatic voltage regulation in mine networks
entry.dc:creator: KOMLEV VP
entry.prism:publicationName: Izv Vyssh Ucheb Zaved Gorn Zh
entry.dc:description: The use of thyristors for voltage regulation in open pit mining network is demonstrated. The booster substation circuits are described.

entry.dc:title: Stability in open pit mining. Proceedings of the 1st International Conference, Vancouver, BC, Nov 23- 25 1970
entry.dc:creator: BRAWNER ED CO
entry.prism:publicationName: Soc of Mining Eng of AIME
entry.dc:description: Proceedings contains 11 papers, minutes of a panel discussion, and a conference summary. Covered in papers topics were- slope stability in the economics, design, and operation of surface mines; geologic factors controling slope stability; influence of rock structure, groundwater, blasting and earthquakes on stability of rock slopes; method of analysis of rock slopes and field instrumentation; design and construction of tailings dams; and case studies of stability in mining projects. Individual papers are provided with bibliographic references.

entry.dc:title: Contribution to the general theory of open pit mining parameters
entry.dc:creator: ONISHCHENKO YUA
entry.prism:publicationName: Izv Vyssh Ucheb Zaved Gorn Zh
entry.dc:description: Analysis of geophysical, and of other factors to be taken into consideration for planing operations in mining, is presented.
